cefrAlignment: Matches B1 (CEFR CV overall reading comprehension and reading for information: straightforward factual texts on familiar topics, with enough understanding to follow how sentences link): 264–269-word passages in plain English, and pronoun and whole-idea reference (this, such, which) at a level B1 readers can manage.
examFidelity: Reference questions fit TOEFL Read an Academic Passage ('connection between ideas' in exams.ts). The email gap task is a sensible reference-word version of TOEIC Part 6. The sentence-completion gaps use a clear IELTS-style word limit, and every answer fits it.
fixes: Moved the correct option in four reference MCQs (ex1 q3 and q5, ex2 q4 and q5). Before this, most keys sat in position B, so learners could spot a pattern.
openConcerns: ex2 q6: 'most of them' grammatically follows 'emails'. The key (customers) depends on the meaning test the lesson teaches, and the explanation says so. This is fine, but it is a harder item.
learnerOutcome: A learner can trace it, they, this, which and such back to the right noun or idea, use them to order sentences, and choose the right pronoun or determiner in a text-completion gap.
